title: Loops, Arrays, and Bounds
summary: Use for, while, arrays, indexes, accumulators, break, continue, and invariants that prevent out-of-bounds access.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Loops, Arrays, and Bounds
Compile and test behavior with warnings enabled
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: C arrays contain a fixed number of adjacent elements and do not carry their length into a called function. Valid indexes run from zero through length minus one. Compute a local array count with `sizeof array / sizeof array[0]` only where `array` is still an array, not a pointer parameter. Use `size_t` for sizes and indexes. A loop invariant states what remains valid before each iteration; conditions such as `i < count` protect bounds. Out-of-range access is undefined behavior, not a guaranteed exception.
keyPoints: C arrays contain a fixed number of adjacent elements and do not carry their length into a called function.
commonMistakes: missing break can execute later cases
index equal to count is out of bounds
